**variant-check** now checks onboarding variants too, not only paywalls.

Give it the onboarding flow of version A and version B (Figma frames, screenshots, a prototype or a description, screens in order up to the first paywall and what follows its close) and the test plan (trial starts or paid conversion per new user, and the smallest change the test can see, e.g. from https://planner.theoutlines.xyz). It says:

- which of 16 onboarding mechanics B changes: value promise on screen 1, outcome copy, goal questions, a plan built from the answers, the loader, core action first, flow length, social proof before the ask, sign-up later, reminder set-up, commitment, paywall position, a paywall that echoes the answers, a value step before the plans, one-tap trial, a second offer after the paywall closes;
- whether published tests moved numbers enough for this test to see it, as built and if built like the winning versions. Calls that rest only on bundled or directional tests stop at "maybe"; changes whose published results are losses (cutting the flow, a loader with no real plan after it) are called "likely to lose";
- flow checks: who reaches the paywall, tactics that flip sign across the onboarding-paywall seam, trial starts vs paid;
- onboarding screen flags (permission pre-prompts, sourced health numbers, real proof, honest progress and loaders);
- a clarity pretest per mechanic.

Paywall checks are unchanged, with two clarifications: one issue caps a call once, and per-month breakdowns round up, never down.

QA: two rounds of two independent runs on the same three briefs (two onboarding, one paywall). In round 2 all verdicts and overall calls matched.

One zip per skill below.
